title: Trade and How Prices Are Set
summary: Why countries trade, and how supply and demand set the price of a mango.

steps.title: Why trade?
sentences: India grows spices and tea, while some countries have oil or make advanced machines.
By trading, each place can sell what it does best and buy what it lacks.

steps.title: Supply and demand
sentences: Supply is how much of something is for sale, and demand is how much people want to buy.
In mango season there are many mangoes, so the price falls.
Out of season there are few, and many people still want them, so the price goes up.

steps.title: Prices send signals
sentences: A high price tells sellers to bring more and tells buyers to use less.
A low price does the opposite.
That is how a market, a place where people trade, balances itself without anybody giving orders.

steps.title: Real life
sentences: Prices also depend on the cost of making and carrying a thing, taxes and quality.
Governments sometimes set limits on prices of important things like medicines.
Learning to compare prices helps you spend wisely.

facts: India is among the world's largest producers of milk, pulses and spices.
Ancient Tamil traders sold pepper, pearls and cloth to Rome more than 2,000 years ago.
Items that are rare and wanted by many, like gold, tend to have high prices.

quiz.q: What happens to price when supply is high and demand is the same?
quiz.why: More supply means a lower price.

options: How much people want to buy
How much a thing costs to make
To get what they lack and sell what they have
quiz.why: Trade shares what each place has.
